label: Outlook
description: Search and read mail, draft and send messages, and manage calendar events, contacts, and To Do tasks.
securityDescription: Microsoft sign-in opens through Composio. Agents can read the mail, calendars, contacts, and To Do lists the connected account can reach. With write access, Agents can send email to any address, as Gmail can, reply to a message's sender, create drafts and draft replies, send drafts, accept invitations, create and update events, mark, flag, and categorize messages, and create contacts and tasks. Agents cannot forward mail, reply to all, add CC or BCC to a reply, send as another mailbox, add or change event attendees, decline or cancel events, move, copy, or delete mail, download attachments or attach files, create mail rules, or change mailbox settings.

drop.OUTLOOK_ADD_MAIL_ATTACHMENT: File uploads are unsupported and inline bytes are capped near 15 KB, so it cannot attach a real file; contentLocation would attach an arbitrary URL reference.

capabilities.description: Accepts or tentatively accepts a calendar meeting invite on behalf of a user. Use this action when a user has received a meeting invitation and wants to indicate their attendance status (either confirmed or tentative). The organizer will receive a notification of the acceptance unless send_response is set to false.

withheldArguments.user_id: changes sharing, visibility, permissions, membership, or who acts
withheldArguments.response_type: changes sharing, visibility, permissions, membership, or who acts

comment.description: Optional text message to include with the response, sent to the organizer.

event_id.description: The unique identifier of the calendar event to respond to.

send_response.description: Whether to send the response to the organizer. Set to false to accept without notifying.

input.description: Request model for accepting or tentatively accepting a calendar meeting invite.

capabilities.description: Creates a new Outlook calendar event, ensuring `start_datetime` is chronologically before `end_datetime`.

withheldArguments.user_id: changes sharing, visibility, permissions, membership, or who acts
withheldArguments.attendees_info: names an address a message goes to or comes from

body.description: The body of the event. This can be in plain text or HTML format, as specified by the 'is_html' field. Optional - events can be created without a body.

is_html.description: Specifies whether the 'body' content is HTML. Set to true for HTML content; otherwise, it's treated as plain text.

show_as.description: The status to show on the calendar for the duration of the event. Valid values are: 'free', 'tentative', 'busy', 'oof' (out of office), 'workingElsewhere', 'unknown'.

subject.description: The subject of the calendar event.

location.description: The physical location of the event.

time_zone.description: The time zone for the start and end times of the event. Uses Windows time zone names (e.g., 'Pacific Standard Time') or IANA time zone names (e.g., 'America/Los_Angeles'). UTC is also a valid input.

categories.description: A list of category names to associate with the event. The API accepts any string values. For best compatibility with Outlook UI color-coding, use category names from the user's master category list. Category names are case-insensitive and duplicates will be automatically removed.

importance.description: The importance of the event. Valid values are 'low', 'normal', 'high'. Defaults to 'normal'.

is_all_day.description: Set to true for an all-day event. When true, start_datetime and end_datetime must both be at midnight and use the same time_zone.

type.description: The recurrence range. The possible values are: endDate, noEnd, numbered.

endDate.description: The date to stop applying the recurrence pattern. Depending on the recurrence pattern of the event, the last occurrence of the meeting may not be this date. Required if type is endDate.

startDate.description: The date to start applying the recurrence pattern. The first occurrence of the meeting may be this date or later, depending on the recurrence pattern of the event. Must be the same value as the start property of the recurring event.

recurrenceTimeZone.description: Time zone for the startDate and endDate properties. Optional. If not specified, the time zone of the event is used.

numberOfOccurrences.description: The number of times to repeat the event. Required and must be positive if type is numbered.

range.description: The duration of a recurring event.

type.description: The recurrence pattern type: daily, weekly, absoluteMonthly, relativeMonthly, absoluteYearly, relativeYearly.

index.description: Specifies on which instance of the allowed days specified in daysOfWeek the event occurs, counted from the first instance in the month. The possible values are: first, second, third, fourth, last. Default is first. Optional and used if type is relativeMonthly or relativeYearly.

month.description: The month in which the event occurs. This is a number from 1 to 12.

interval.description: The number of units between occurrences, where units can be in days, weeks, months, or years, depending on the type.

dayOfMonth.description: The day of the month on which the event occurs. Required if type is absoluteMonthly or absoluteYearly.

daysOfWeek.description: A collection of the days of the week on which the event occurs. The possible values are: sunday, monday, tuesday, wednesday, thursday, friday, saturday. If type is relativeMonthly or relativeYearly, and daysOfWeek specifies morethan one day, the event falls on the first day that satisfies the pattern. Required if type is weekly, relativeMonthly, or relativeYearly.

firstDayOfWeek.description: The first day of the week. The possible values are: sunday, monday, tuesday, wednesday, thursday, friday, saturday. Default is sunday. Required if type is weekly.

pattern.description: The frequency of a recurring event.

recurrence.description: The recurrence pattern and range for an event.

calendar_id.description: The ID of a specific calendar to create the event in. Obtainable from the list calendars action. If omitted, the event is created on the user's default calendar.

end_datetime.description: The event's end date and time. Prefer local YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS with the IANA or Windows zone in time_zone. Z or a numeric offset is accepted only when it agrees with time_zone.

start_datetime.description: The event's start date and time. Prefer local YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS with the IANA or Windows zone in time_zone. Z or a numeric offset is accepted only when it agrees with time_zone.

is_online_meeting.description: Set to true to indicate that the event is an online meeting. This will automatically generate an online meeting link if 'online_meeting_provider' is set (e.g., a Microsoft Teams link).

online_meeting_provider.description: Specifies the online meeting provider. Currently, only 'teamsForBusiness' is supported. If 'is_online_meeting' is true and this is set, a meeting link for the provider will be created.

input.description: Defines the request schema for creating a new event in an Outlook calendar.

capabilities.description: Creates a new contact in a Microsoft Outlook user's contacts folder.

withheldArguments.userId: changes sharing, visibility, permissions, membership, or who acts

notes.description: Personal notes about the contact. These notes are stored as 'personalNotes' in the Outlook contact details.

birthday.description: The contact's birthday in 'YYYY-MM-DD' format. The time component will be set to midnight UTC (e.g., '1990-01-01' becomes '1990-01-01T00:00:00Z' in the API request).

homePhone.description: The contact's home phone number. If provided, this will be stored in Outlook as a list containing this single number.

categories.description: A list of categories to assign to the contact.

department.description: The department the contact belongs to within their company.

companyName.description: The name of the company the contact is associated with.

displayName.description: The contact's display name, typically their full name.

businessPhones.description: A list of business phone numbers for the contact. Each number should be a string.

name.description: The display name for the contact's email address.

emailAddresses.description: A list of email addresses for the contact. Each item must be an object with an `address` field (string) and optionally a `name` field (e.g., `[{'address': 'jane@example.com', 'name': 'Jane Doe'}]`). Plain strings are not accepted.

capabilities.description: Creates a new Outlook email draft with subject, body, recipients, and an optional attachment. This action creates a standalone draft for new conversations. To create a draft reply to an existing conversation/message, use the OUTLOOK_CREATE_DRAFT_REPLY action instead.

withheldArguments.user_id: changes sharing, visibility, permissions, membership, or who acts

body.description: Content of the email draft; use `is_html` to specify if HTML or plain text.

is_html.description: Specifies if the `body` is HTML. If `False`, `body` is plain text. Set to `True` when `body` contains HTML markup; otherwise markup renders as literal text.

subject.description: Subject line for the email draft.

cc_recipients.description: Optional list of CC (carbon copy) recipient email addresses. Must be provided as an array of strings, e.g., ["cc@example.com"].

to_recipients.description: Optional list of primary 'To' recipient email addresses. Must be provided as an array of strings, e.g., ["user@example.com"] for a single recipient or ["user1@example.com", "user2@example.com"] for multiple recipients. Do not pass as a JSON-encoded string. Can be omitted when creating a draft to be completed later. To send the draft, at least one valid address must be present across `to_recipients`, `cc_recipients`, or `bcc_recipients`.

bcc_recipients.description: Optional list of BCC (blind carbon copy) recipient email addresses. Must be provided as an array of strings, e.g., ["bcc@example.com"].

capabilities.description: Creates a draft reply in the specified user's Outlook mailbox to an existing message (identified by a valid `message_id`), optionally including a `comment` and CC/BCC recipients.

withheldArguments.user_id: changes sharing, visibility, permissions, membership, or who acts
withheldArguments.cc_emails: names an address a message goes to or comes from
withheldArguments.bcc_emails: names an address a message goes to or comes from

comment.description: Plain text comment to include in the body of the reply draft.

message_id.description: Required. Unique ID of the message to reply to. Obtain this from actions like 'List Messages', 'Get Message', or 'Search Messages'.

capabilities.description: Tool to create a new task in Microsoft To Do within a specified task list. Use when adding tasks with title, due dates, reminders, importance levels, descriptions, categories, and linked resources.

withheldArguments.user_id: changes sharing, visibility, permissions, membership, or who acts

content.description: The content of the task body.

contentType.description: The type of the content. Use 'text' for plain text or 'html' for HTML formatted content.

body.description: Task body content with content type.

title.description: The title of the task. This is the main text displayed for the task.

categories.description: A list of category labels to organize the task (e.g., tags for filtering or grouping tasks).

importance.description: The importance level of the task. Must be one of: 'low', 'normal', or 'high'. Defaults to 'normal' if not specified.

dateTime.description: A single point of time in ISO 8601 format (e.g., 2024-01-15T14:30:00). Do not include timezone offset in the string itself.

timeZone.description: Time zone designation. Use standard IANA time zone identifiers (e.g., 'America/New_York', 'Europe/London') or 'UTC' for Coordinated Universal Time.

dueDateTime.description: Date/time with timezone information for task due dates and reminders.

webUrl.description: URL pointing to the linked resource.

displayName.description: The display name of the linked resource.

applicationName.description: The application name of the source that created the linked resource.

items.description: Resource linked to the task (e.g., document, email, or web link).

linkedResources.description: A list of resources (documents, links, emails) associated with the task. Each resource can have a webUrl, applicationName, and displayName.

dateTime.description: A single point of time in ISO 8601 format (e.g., 2024-01-15T14:30:00). Do not include timezone offset in the string itself.

timeZone.description: Time zone designation. Use standard IANA time zone identifiers (e.g., 'America/New_York', 'Europe/London') or 'UTC' for Coordinated Universal Time.

reminderDateTime.description: Date/time with timezone information for task due dates and reminders.

todo_task_list_id.description: The unique identifier of the task list where the task will be created. Use the List To Do task lists action to retrieve available list IDs.

capabilities.description: Suggests meeting times based on organizer and attendee availability, time constraints, and duration requirements. Use when you need to find optimal meeting slots across multiple participants' schedules.

user_id.description: User ID or User Principal Name. Use 'me' for the authenticated user.

emailAddress.description: Email address information for the attendee.

items.description: Represents an attendee or resource for the meeting.

attendees.description: List of attendees or resources for the meeting. Empty list searches only organizer's availability.

max_candidates.description: Maximum number of meeting time suggestions to return.

prefer_timezone.description: Preferred timezone for the response (sets Prefer header with outlook.timezone). If not specified, defaults to UTC.

activityDomain.description: Nature of activity. Valid values: 'work' (Mon-Fri 8am-5pm, default), 'personal' (Mon-Sun 8am-5pm), 'unrestricted' (24/7), 'unknown'.

meeting_duration.description: Meeting length in ISO 8601 duration format (e.g., 'PT1H' for 1 hour, 'PT30M' for 30 minutes). Default: 30 minutes.

resolveAvailability.description: If true, check if the location is available.

isRequired.description: If true, a location is required for the meeting.

is_organizer_optional.description: If true, organizer doesn't need to attend. Default: false.

return_suggestion_reasons.description: If true, include reasons for each suggestion. Default: false.

minimum_attendee_percentage.description: Minimum confidence percentage (0-100) for suggestions. Default: 50.

input.description: Request schema for finding meeting times.

capabilities.description: Get events ACTIVE during a time window (includes multi-day events). Use for "what's on my calendar today/this week" or availability checks. Returns events overlapping the time range. For keyword search or filters by category, use OUTLOOK_LIST_EVENTS instead.

top.description: Maximum number of events to retrieve.

skip.description: Number of events to skip before returning the page (OData $skip).

select.description: List of event properties to return. Defaults to commonly-needed fields excluding the full HTML body. To include the full body content, explicitly add 'body' to this list.

orderby.description: OData ordering expression for events, for example 'start/dateTime asc'.

user_id.description: Email address of the target user (or 'me' for authenticated user).

timezone.description: Timezone for event times in the response only; the input window is always interpreted from the offset in start_datetime/end_datetime. Must be an IANA timezone name (e.g., 'America/New_York', 'Europe/London', 'Asia/Kolkata') or Windows timezone identifier (e.g., 'Pacific Standard Time', 'India Standard Time'). UTC offsets like '+05:30' or 'GMT+5' are NOT supported. Defaults to UTC.

page_token.description: Opaque continuation token for the next page. Omit for the first page; then pass back the `next_page_token` from the previous response, unmodified, until it is absent. Do not construct or edit it. When set, it drives pagination; resend any required identifier fields from the first call (the token supersedes their values). Optional filter, sort and timezone params need not be repeated; the token carries them.

calendar_id.description: Optional ID of a specific calendar to query. Must be a calendar identifier (format like 'AAMkAGI2TG93AAA='), NOT an email address. If not provided, uses the primary calendar. Get calendar IDs using LIST_CALENDARS action.

end_datetime.description: The end date and time of the time range, represented in ISO 8601 format. For example, '2019-11-08T20:00:00-08:00' or '2024-12-31T23:59:59Z'.

start_datetime.description: The start date and time of the time range, represented in ISO 8601 format. For example, '2019-11-08T19:00:00-08:00' or '2024-01-01T00:00:00Z'.

include_sensitivity_label.description: When true, retrieves and normalizes the Microsoft Purview sensitivity label applied to each calendar event. This is distinct from the event's built-in sensitivity field and any Teams meeting label. Preserved in next_page_token.

capabilities.description: Retrieves the full details of a specific calendar event by its ID from a user's Outlook calendar, provided the event exists.

user_id.description: The user's primary SMTP address, user principal name (UPN), or the alias 'me' (for the signed-in user) to identify the calendar owner.

event_id.description: The unique identifier of the calendar event to retrieve.

include_sensitivity_label.description: When true, retrieves and normalizes the event's Microsoft Purview sensitivity label from a filtered msip_labels expansion in the same Graph request. This is distinct from the event's built-in sensitivity field and from a Teams online meeting sensitivity-label assignment. Requires Calendars.Read or Calendars.ReadWrite. Treat a returned status of unknown as fail-closed before using the event content.

capabilities.description: Retrieve incremental changes (delta) of messages in a mailbox. FIRST RUN: Returns ALL messages in folder (use top=50 to limit). Response has @odata.deltaLink. SUBSEQUENT: Pass stored deltaLink to get only NEW/UPDATED/DELETED messages since last sync. Properties available: id, subject, from, receivedDateTime, isRead, etc. NOT available: internetMessageHeaders, full body, attachment content (response size limits).

top.description: Maximum number of items to return per page. For first run without delta_token, use top=50 or top=100 to limit results. First delta call without token returns all messages in folder. Paginate through results using @odata.nextLink, then store @odata.deltaLink for next sync.

items.description: Valid navigation properties that can be expanded in delta queries. Only navigation properties (relationships) can be expanded. Regular properties like body, from, toRecipients, etc. are NOT expandable and will cause API errors. Note: 'extensions' is technically a navigation property but requires complex OData filter syntax (e.g., $expand=extensions($filter=id eq 'ExtensionId')) which is not supported by this simple expand parameter.

expand.description: Navigation properties to expand inline. Supported values: 'attachments', 'multiValueExtendedProperties', 'singleValueExtendedProperties'. Regular properties (body, from, toRecipients, etc.) cannot be expanded and will cause errors.

select.description: List of message properties to include (e.g. ['subject','receivedDateTime']). Delta sync has property limitations due to response size constraints. Not available in delta: internetMessageHeaders, body (full), attachments (full content). Available: id, subject, from, toRecipients, ccRecipients, bccRecipients, receivedDateTime, sentDateTime, isRead, isDraft, importance, hasAttachments, categories, conversationId, flag, webLink, bodyPreview (first 255 chars).

user_id.description: User identifier: 'me' for the signed-in user or the user's email/UPN.

folder_id.description: Mail folder identifier (folder GUID) or well-known folder name. Well-known names (case-insensitive): 'inbox', 'drafts', 'sentitems', 'deleteditems', 'junkemail', 'outbox', 'archive', 'clutter', 'conversationhistory'. For custom folders, use the folder ID GUID from LIST_MAIL_FOLDERS. Defaults to 'inbox' when omitted.

skip_token.description: Skip token for paging through large result sets during initial sync. Accepts either the full @odata.nextLink URL or just the bare token value. Keep paginating until you receive '@odata.deltaLink' instead of nextLink. When using sensitivity-label enrichment, resend include_sensitivity_label=true with this token. Mutually exclusive with delta_token - only one should be provided per request.

delta_token.description: Delta token from a previous call to get only changes since that state. Accepts either the full @odata.deltaLink URL or just the bare token value. If omitted or invalid (placeholders like <token> are ignored), performs initial sync. Use top parameter on first run to limit results. Response includes @odata.deltaLink - store this for subsequent calls. When using sensitivity-label enrichment, resend include_sensitivity_label=true with this token.

include_sensitivity_label.description: When true, retrieves and normalizes Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels for delta items through Microsoft Graph JSON batches capped at 20 requests per batch. Requires Mail.Read. Treat status unknown as fail-closed before using message content. Repeat this flag on every call that uses skip_token or delta_token because Graph tokens do not preserve this Composio-only setting.

input.description: Request schema for retrieving incremental changes (delta) of messages in a mailbox.

user_id.description: User principal name (UPN) or 'me' for the signed-in user.

capabilities.description: Retrieves a specific Outlook contact by its `contact_id` from the contacts of a specified `user_id` (defaults to 'me' for the authenticated user).

user_id.description: User's principal name (e.g., 'AdeleV@contoso.onmicrosoft.com') or 'me' for the authenticated user. Using 'me' is recommended for accessing one's own contacts.

contact_id.description: Unique identifier for the contact within the specified user's Outlook address book.

capabilities.description: Retrieve a message by immutable ID from the specified Outlook mailbox. Use `select` to include fields such as `internetMessageHeaders`. A 404 can indicate a deleted message, a different mailbox, or a stale legacy mutable ID.

select.description: List of message properties to include in the response. Can be provided as an array of strings (e.g., ['subject', 'body']) or as a comma-separated string (e.g., 'subject,body'). Reduces data transfer and improves performance. Common fields: id, subject, from, toRecipients, ccRecipients, receivedDateTime, sentDateTime, body, bodyPreview, hasAttachments, webLink, internetMessageHeaders, isRead, importance, categories. Leave empty to return all message fields.

user_id.description: User's email address, UPN, or 'me' for the currently authenticated user.

message_id.description: Unique immutable ID of the Outlook email message to retrieve. Accepts message IDs from OUTLOOK_LIST_MESSAGES (message.id), OUTLOOK_QUERY_EMAILS (message.id), or OUTLOOK_SEARCH_MESSAGES (use hitId from search results, as resource.id is not populated by the Search API). The message must exist in the specified user's mailbox. Legacy mutable IDs can become stale after a folder move.

include_sensitivity_label.description: When true, retrieves and normalizes the message's Microsoft Purview sensitivity label in the same Graph request. Requires Mail.Read or Mail.ReadWrite. Treat a returned status of unknown as fail-closed before using the message content.

capabilities.description: Retrieves the Microsoft Outlook profile for a specified user.

user_id.description: The user's unique identifier or principal name. Use 'me' to get the profile of the authenticated user.

include_proxy_addresses.description: Whether to include proxy addresses in the response. Proxy addresses are SMTP addresses prefixed with 'SMTP:' (primary) or 'smtp:' (secondary).

capabilities.description: Retrieves user details from Microsoft Graph by email address (userPrincipalName). Returns user properties including display name, job title, department, and contact information. Use this action when you need to look up a user's profile information using their email address.

email.description: The email address (userPrincipalName) of the user to retrieve. This must be a valid email address format.

select.description: Optional list of user properties to include in the response. Reduces data transfer and improves performance. Common fields: id, displayName, givenName, surname, mail, userPrincipalName, jobTitle, officeLocation, mobilePhone, businessPhones, department. Leave empty to return default properties.

input.description: Request model for getting a user by email address.

capabilities.description: Tool to retrieve a specific calendar event from a user's primary calendar. Use when you need detailed information about a particular event for a given user.

user_id.description: The user's primary SMTP address, user principal name (UPN), or user ID to identify the calendar owner whose event you want to retrieve.

event_id.description: The unique identifier of the calendar event to retrieve from the user's calendar.

include_sensitivity_label.description: When true, retrieves and normalizes the event's Microsoft Purview sensitivity label from a filtered msip_labels expansion in the same Graph request. This is distinct from the event's built-in sensitivity field and from a Teams online meeting sensitivity-label assignment. Requires Calendars.Read or Calendars.ReadWrite. Treat a returned status of unknown as fail-closed before using the event content.

capabilities.description: Tool to list calendars in the signed-in user's mailbox. Use when you need to retrieve calendars with optional OData queries.

top.description: Maximum number of calendars to return (OData $top).

user_id.description: User ID or userPrincipalName. Use 'me' for the signed-in user.

page_token.description: Opaque continuation token for the next page. Omit for the first page; then pass back the `next_page_token` from the previous response, unmodified, until it is absent. Do not construct or edit it. When set, it drives pagination; resend any required identifier fields from the first call (the token supersedes their values). Optional filter, sort and timezone params need not be repeated; the token carries them.

capabilities.description: Retrieves events from a user's Outlook calendar via Microsoft Graph API. Supports primary/secondary/shared calendars, pagination, filtering, property selection, sorting, and timezone specification. Use calendar_id to access non-primary calendars.

top.description: Maximum number of events to retrieve per page for pagination.

skip.description: Number of initial events to bypass, used for pagination.

filter.description: OData query string to filter calendar events. Filterable properties: 'start/dateTime', 'end/dateTime', 'subject', 'categories', 'importance', 'sensitivity', 'isAllDay', 'isCancelled', 'isReminderOn', 'type'. CRITICAL: Properties like 'body', 'bodyPreview', 'location', 'organizer', 'attendees' do NOT support $filter. Do NOT use mail properties like 'receivedDateTime' (emails only).

select.description: List of specific event property names to return. MUST be provided as a list. If omitted, a default set of properties is returned. Valid field names: id, subject, body, bodyPreview, start, end, isAllDay, organizer, attendees, location, locations, recurrence, importance, sensitivity, showAs, categories, hasAttachments, webLink, onlineMeeting, onlineMeetingProvider, onlineMeetingUrl, isOnlineMeeting, createdDateTime, lastModifiedDateTime, changeKey, iCalUId, type, seriesMasterId, isOrganizer,

orderby.description: List of properties to sort results by. Each item is a string like 'start/dateTime desc' or 'subject asc'. MUST be provided as a list, even for single sort criteria. Use 'asc' (default) or 'desc' for order. IMPORTANT: Use calendar event properties ONLY. Do NOT use mail/message properties like 'receivedDateTime' (which is for emails only). Valid sortable datetime fields: 'start/dateTime', 'end/dateTime', 'createdDateTime', 'lastModifiedDateTime'.

user_id.description: Email address of the target user (or 'me' for authenticated user), identifying the calendar for event listing.

timezone.description: Preferred timezone for event start/end times. Accepts IANA format (e.g., 'America/New_York', 'Europe/London', 'Indian/Mauritius', 'Asia/Tokyo') or Windows format (e.g., 'Eastern Standard Time', 'Pacific Standard Time'). Placeholder patterns like '<REGION>/London' are auto-resolved to valid IANA timezones (e.g., 'Europe/London') where the city can be matched. Falls back to 'UTC' only if the timezone cannot be resolved.

page_token.description: Opaque continuation token for the next page. Omit for the first page; then pass back the `next_page_token` from the previous response, unmodified, until it is absent. Do not construct or edit it. When set, it drives pagination; resend any required identifier fields from the first call (the token supersedes their values). Optional filter, sort and timezone params need not be repeated; the token carries them. Not available together with expand_recurring_events.

calendar_id.description: Optional ID of a specific calendar to retrieve events from. If not provided, uses the default calendar. Get calendar IDs using LIST_CALENDARS action. IMPORTANT: Do NOT use 'primary' or 'default' as values - these are not valid calendar IDs in Microsoft Graph. Leave this field empty/null to access the default calendar. Useful for accessing secondary calendars, shared calendars, or team calendars.

expand_recurring_events.description: When true, automatically expands recurring events to show actual occurrences within the filtered date range instead of series masters. When false (default), returns series masters as before.

include_sensitivity_label.description: When true, retrieves and normalizes the Microsoft Purview sensitivity label stored on each calendar event. This is distinct from the event's built-in sensitivity field and from a Teams online meeting sensitivity label.

capabilities.description: Compatibility action that lists messages directly contained in one specified mail folder. It does not recursively include messages from descendant folders. Prefer OUTLOOK_LIST_MESSAGES for new calls; use this action only when its $expand support is required.

top.description: Maximum number of messages to return per request (1-1000). To page through more, use the `next_page_token` from the response (pass it back as `page_token`).

skip.description: Number of messages to skip from the beginning of the result set, for pagination.

expand.description: List of message navigation properties to include inline using OData $expand. Use Graph expansion expressions such as 'attachments' or 'attachments($select=id,name,size,contentType,isInline)'. Regular message properties belong in select, not expand.

filter.description: OData $filter query to filter messages. CRITICAL: String literals MUST use single quotes ('), not double quotes ("). Examples: 'isRead eq false', 'from/emailAddress/address eq 'sender@example.com'', 'receivedDateTime ge 2023-01-01T00:00:00Z', 'hasAttachments eq true'.

select.description: List of message properties to include in the response. OData $select parameter. Valid properties include: id, subject, from, toRecipients, receivedDateTime, sentDateTime, hasAttachments, importance, isRead, body, bodyPreview, categories, conversationId.

orderby.description: Property to sort results by with direction. OData $orderby parameter. Example: 'receivedDateTime desc' or 'subject asc'. IMPORTANT: Cannot be used with complex 'filter' queries (multiple 'contains()' operations, OR clauses, or nested properties like 'from/emailAddress/address') - Microsoft Graph will reject such combinations with InefficientFilter error. For complex filters, omit this parameter and sort results client-side.

user_id.description: User's id, userPrincipalName, or 'me' for the signed-in user.

page_token.description: Opaque continuation token for the next page. Omit for the first page; then pass back the `next_page_token` from the previous response, unmodified, until it is absent. Do not construct or edit it. When set, it drives pagination; resend any required identifier fields from the first call (the token supersedes their values). body.description: New body content (Text or HTML). If omitted, the existing message body remains unchanged. Must be a dict with both `contentType` ('Text' or 'HTML') and `content` keys set together; omitting `contentType` defaults to plain text and will not render HTML markup.

flagStatus.description: Flag status for the message. Possible values: 'notFlagged', 'flagged', 'complete'. When 'notFlagged', any date/time fields (startDateTime, dueDateTime, completedDateTime) are ignored.

dateTime.description: A single point of time in a combined date and time representation ({date}T{time}; for example, 2017-08-29T04:00:00.0000000).

timeZone.description: Represents a time zone, for example, 'Pacific Standard Time' or 'UTC'.

dueDateTime.description: Represents a date and time with timezone information for input.

dateTime.description: A single point of time in a combined date and time representation ({date}T{time}; for example, 2017-08-29T04:00:00.0000000).

timeZone.description: Represents a time zone, for example, 'Pacific Standard Time' or 'UTC'.

startDateTime.description: Represents a date and time with timezone information for input.

dateTime.description: A single point of time in a combined date and time representation ({date}T{time}; for example, 2017-08-29T04:00:00.0000000).

timeZone.description: Represents a time zone, for example, 'Pacific Standard Time' or 'UTC'.

completedDateTime.description: Represents a date and time with timezone information for input.

flag.description: Represents the flag value for a message (input).

is_read.description: Mark message as read (True) or unread (False). If omitted, read status remains unchanged.

subject.description: New subject line. If omitted, the existing subject remains unchanged. Provide empty string to clear the subject.

categories.description: Categories associated with the message. Provides a list of category labels (e.g., 'Follow Up', 'Customer').

importance.description: New importance level ('low', 'normal', 'high'). If omitted, the existing importance level remains unchanged.

message_id.description: The unique identifier of the email message to be updated. This ID is typically obtained from listing messages or creating/sending a message. URL-encoded IDs are automatically decoded before use.

internet_message_id.description: The message ID in the format specified by RFC2822. Updatable only if isDraft = true.

inference_classification.description: Classification of the message for the user based on inferred relevance or importance. Possible values: 'focused' or 'other'.

is_read_receipt_requested.description: Indicates whether a read receipt is requested for the message.

is_delivery_receipt_requested.description: Indicates whether a delivery receipt is requested for the message.

capabilities.description: Tool to update an existing task in Microsoft To Do. Use when modifying a task's title, status, importance, due date, reminder, body, or categories. Only the fields you provide will be changed.

withheldArguments.user_id: changes sharing, visibility, permissions, membership, or who acts

content.description: The content of the task body.

contentType.description: The type of the content. Use 'text' for plain text or 'html' for HTML formatted content.

body.description: Updated description or notes for the task. Provide both contentType ('text' or 'html') and content fields.

title.description: The new title of the task.

status.description: The updated status of the task. Allowed values: 'notStarted', 'inProgress', 'completed', 'waitingOnOthers', 'deferred'.

task_id.description: The unique identifier of the task to update. Obtain this from List To Do tasks or Create To Do task.

categories.description: Updated list of category labels for the task.

importance.description: The importance level of the task. Allowed values: 'low', 'normal', 'high'.

dateTime.description: A single point of time in ISO 8601 format (e.g., 2024-01-15T14:30:00). Do not include timezone offset in the string itself.

timeZone.description: Time zone designation. Use standard IANA time zone identifiers (e.g., 'America/New_York', 'Europe/London') or 'UTC'.

dueDateTime.description: The updated due date and time. Provide both dateTime (ISO 8601) and timeZone.

dateTime.description: A single point of time in ISO 8601 format (e.g., 2024-01-15T14:30:00). Do not include timezone offset in the string itself.

timeZone.description: Time zone designation. Use standard IANA time zone identifiers (e.g., 'America/New_York', 'Europe/London') or 'UTC'.

reminderDateTime.description: The updated reminder date and time. Setting this will also enable the reminder.

dateTime.description: A single point of time in ISO 8601 format (e.g., 2024-01-15T14:30:00). Do not include timezone offset in the string itself.

timeZone.description: Time zone designation. Use standard IANA time zone identifiers (e.g., 'America/New_York', 'Europe/London') or 'UTC'.

completedDateTime.description: The date and time the task was completed. Typically set alongside status='completed'.

todo_task_list_id.description: The unique identifier of the task list that contains the task.

capabilities.description: Return the identity (email, name) of the connected Outlook account.

input.description: The current connected account's identity. Takes no parameters.
